chunks.arabic_text: رِجَالُ الْكَشِّيِّ: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ قُولَوَيْهَ، عَنْ سَعْدٍ، عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى، عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ الْحَجَّالِ، عَنِ الْعَلَاءِ، عَنِ ابْنِ أَبِي يَعْفُورَ قَالَ

translations.en: Rijal al-Kashshi: Muhammad ibn Qulawayh, from Sa'd, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Abdallah al-Hajjal, from al-Ala, from Ibn Abi Ya'fur who said:

chunks.arabic_text: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَام إِنَّ لَيْسَ كُلَّ سَاعَةٍ أَلْقَاكَ وَلَا يُمْكِنُ الْقُدُومَ، وَيَجِيءُ الرَّجُلُ مِنْ أَصْحَابِنَا فَيَسْأَلُنِي وَلَيْسَ عِنْدِي كُلُّمَا يَسْأَلُنِي عَنْهُ، قَالَ: فَمَا يَمْنَعُكَ مِنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ الثَّقَفِيِّ فَإِنَّهُ قَدْ سَمِعَ مِنْ أَبِي وَكَانَ عِنْدَهُ وَجِيهًا

translations.en: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'I do not meet you at all times, and it is not always possible to travel (to come to you). A man from among our companions comes and asks me, but I do not have everything regarding what he asks me about.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'What prevents you from (going to) Muhammad ibn Muslim al-Thaqafi? For he had heard from my father and had a most favorable position with him.'

en.summary: This hadith from Al-Kashi’s *Rijal* underscores the Shia principle of *Tawassul* through knowledgeable companions (*A'yan*) when direct access to the Imam is limited. By recommending Muhammad ibn al-Musanna al-Thaqafi, who was 'close' (*wajihan*) to the Prophet’s family, the Imam validates the authority of solitary reports (*Khabar al-Wahid*) from trustworthy narrators as a reliable source of religious law. This establishes a historical precedent for the scholarly hierarchy and the reliance on *Ahl al-Bayt*’s direct disciples in the absence of the Imam.
en.seo_question: Why did the Imam recommend Muhammad ibn Muslim al-Thaqafi for answering religious questions?
